title: Banking and Credit Fundamentals
summary: Learn how banks work, accounts and payments, simple and compound interest, loans and repayments, fraud protection and banking ethics.
audience: Students, new bank staff and anyone who wants to use banking services with confidence

lessons.title: What banks do and the types of bank

body.p: A bank takes deposits from people and businesses who have spare money and lends to those who need it. It earns by charging more interest on loans than it pays on deposits, plus fees. This role as a go-between is called financial intermediation. It also gives safe storage for money and a way to make payments.

list: Retail or commercial banks serve individuals and small businesses with accounts, cards and loans.
Investment banks advise companies and help them raise money by issuing shares and bonds.
Central banks, such as the Central Bank of Nigeria or the Bank of England, issue currency, set policy interest rates and supervise other banks. They do not normally serve the public.
Microfinance institutions and cooperatives give small loans and savings services, often to people shut out of regular banks.
Mobile money providers move money using phones and agents.

body.p: If many depositors ask for their money at the same time, a bank cannot pay everyone because most deposits are lent out. This is a bank run. To protect trust, regulators set capital and liquidity rules, inspect banks, and many countries run deposit insurance schemes up to a set limit. The details differ by country, so check the limit in yours.

Most people meet banking through accounts. A current or checking account is for everyday payments and may allow overdrafts. A savings account pays interest and may limit withdrawals. A fixed or term deposit locks money for a set period at a higher rate.

list: Cash and cheques for traditional payments.
Debit cards take money straight from your account.
Credit cards lend you money for a short time and charge interest if you do not repay in full by the due date.
Bank transfers and instant payment systems move money between accounts within seconds.
Mobile money and wallet apps hold balances with a provider and move them by phone.

body.p: Banks must confirm who you are before opening an account. This is called KYC. They usually ask for identity documents, proof of address and sometimes a tax or biometric number. The rules exist to stop money laundering and fraud. Keep your documents safe and never lend your account to someone else.

body.tip: Check your statement at least once a month. Report anything you do not recognise to your bank straight away.

body.p: Interest is the price of using money. The rate is stated per year unless said otherwise. Two methods matter.
Simple interest is calculated only on the original amount: I = P x r x t. If you deposit 100,000 at 12% for 3 years, the interest is 100,000 x 0.12 x 3 = 36,000, and you end with 136,000.

With compound interest, interest is added to the balance and earns interest itself. The formula is A = P x (1 + r)^t when added once a year. For the same 100,000 at 12% for 3 years, A = 100,000 x 1.12^3 = 140,492.80, so the interest is 40,492.80. That is 4,492.80 more than simple interest.
Compounding more often adds a little more. At 4% a year compounded monthly, 50,000 grows to 50,000 x (1 + 0.04/12)^12 = 52,037.08 after one year, while annual compounding gives 52,000.00.

Compounding is powerful for savings over long periods and costly for debts that you leave unpaid. A quoted monthly rate of 1% on a loan is not the same as 1% a year. It is 12% a year before compounding.

A loan gives you money now in return for repayments with interest. Before borrowing, find out the interest rate, the term, the fees, whether the rate is fixed or can change, and what happens if you pay late.

Borrow 120,000 at 1% per month over 12 months on a reducing balance (interest each month is charged on what you still owe). The monthly payment comes from the formula P x r / (1 - (1 + r)^-n), which gives 10,661.85. Over 12 months you pay 12 x 10,661.85 = 127,942.26 (rounded), so the total interest is about 7,942. Note how this is lower than a flat 1% per month on the full 120,000, which would be 14,400 of interest.

Secured loans are backed by an asset, such as a house or car, which the lender can take if you default. Unsecured loans, such as most personal loans and credit cards, usually carry higher rates. A guarantor agrees to pay if you cannot, so never sign as a guarantor unless you can afford to pay.
In many countries a credit bureau records your borrowing and repayments. A good record can lower your future rates. Late payments and defaults reduce it for years.

body.tip: Compare loans by the total you will repay and the annual percentage rate (APR), not by the monthly payment alone.

lessons.title: Risk, fraud and protecting your money

body.p: Banks manage several risks. Credit risk is that borrowers do not repay. Liquidity risk is not having enough cash to meet withdrawals. Market risk is losses from changes in interest or exchange rates. Operational risk covers errors, system failures and fraud. Managing these risks is a large part of a banker's job.

list: Phishing: messages that pretend to be from your bank and ask for passwords or one-time codes.
SIM swap: a criminal gets your number transferred so they receive your verification codes.
Fake investment schemes promising high, fast returns.
Advance-fee scams: you must pay a fee first to receive a loan or prize.

steps: Never share your PIN, password or one-time code with anyone, including someone claiming to be the bank.
Use the bank's official app or website, typed yourself.
If a call or message makes you rush, stop and contact the bank on a number you already trust.
Report lost cards or suspicious activity immediately.

lessons.title: Working in banking: roles, ethics and next steps

body.p: Banks employ many kinds of people: tellers and customer service staff, relationship managers, loan officers and credit analysts, risk and compliance officers, auditors, treasury dealers, and technology and data teams. Entry roles often need a diploma or degree and strong numeracy and communication skills.

list: Put customer money and data first. Confidentiality is a legal duty in most countries.
Avoid conflicts of interest and disclose them when they arise.
Follow anti-money-laundering rules and report suspicious transactions as required.
Treat customers fairly and explain products honestly, including costs and risks.

body.p: If you want a banking career, look at the professional bodies in your country, such as institutes of bankers, and at certifications in areas like credit analysis, risk management and compliance. This course gives you a foundation. Qualifications and rules differ from one country to another, so check what your local regulator and employers require.

body.tip: Practise the calculations in this course with real quoted rates from two banks. Working out the true cost of a loan is a skill every employer values.

quiz.q: What is the main way a commercial bank earns income?
options: Charging more on loans than it pays on deposits, plus fees

quiz.q: Which institution usually sets the policy interest rate and supervises banks?
What does KYC stand for in banking?
What is the simple interest on 100,000 at 12% for 3 years?
What is the balance after 3 years if 100,000 earns 12% compound interest, added yearly?
Why is compound interest larger than simple interest over several years?
options: Interest is added to the balance and earns interest itself
It is charged twice a year by law

quiz.q: A loan of 120,000 at 1% a month over 12 months on a reducing balance has a monthly payment of about:
Which is a sign of a phishing attack?
options: Your bank app showing the correct balance
A message asking you to share your one-time code
An alert after you made a payment

quiz.q: Which loan is generally the riskiest for the lender and so usually carries a higher rate?
options: A loan backed by a house

quiz.q: What should you compare when choosing between loans?
options: The colour of the bank brand
The total repayment and the APR
Many depositors withdraw at once and the bank cannot pay everyone from cash

quiz.q: Which is the safest response to a call from someone claiming to be your bank asking for your PIN?
options: Give it to prove you are the account holder
Hang up and call the bank on a number you already trust
